churn_resistance.rationale: Data access is centralized behind one module, config matches the framework template, and only public APIs are used — an upgrade would touch few files. It loses a point for being entirely untyped at the API boundary and for the two small structural warts (formatting in the data layer, status-code-after-stream).

findings.issue: The entire app is untyped JavaScript (.jsx, zero type annotations), so PokeAPI's large, deeply nested response shapes and each query's view model cross every boundary untyped; a renamed or misread field (e.g. version_group_details, sprites.other['official-artwork']) fails only at runtime.
findings.suggestion: Port the four modules to TSX with a small set of interfaces for the API responses and the view models each query returns; SolidStart v2 is TS-first and the existing tsconfig.json (app/tsconfig.json:1) plus "types": ["vite/client", "@solidjs/start/env"] are already half of the setup.

findings.issue: HttpStatusCode 404 is rendered inside <Show when={data() === null}> that only resolves after the async query, which is the pattern of open upstream bug solid-start#2229 (status set after streaming starts is lost); the same shape exists in moves/[name].jsx:52-54, abilities/[name].jsx:28-30, types/[name].jsx:49-51.
findings.suggestion: Pass { deferStream: true } to createAsync for these routes (the documented fix for status/redirect-after-stream) or set the status from the server function, so the 404 survives when the framework's streaming behavior changes.

findings.issue: apiFetch memoizes the promise, so a transient API failure is cached as null for the process lifetime with no retry or TTL.
findings.suggestion: Cache only successful responses (or add a short TTL for failures), keeping the in-memory cache the spec permits.

findings.issue: idFromUrl hand-parses resource URLs with a regex /\/(\d+)\/?$/ instead of the platform URL parser.
findings.suggestion: Use new URL(url).pathname and split, which is more robust and self-documenting.

findings.issue: The game select builds the navigation URL by string interpolation (?game=${value}) without URLSearchParams or encodeURIComponent; safe for kebab-case version-group names today, brittle if names ever differ.
findings.suggestion: Build the href with URLSearchParams like app/src/routes/index.jsx:19-24 does.

findings.issue: Presentation formatting (height/weight as toFixed(1) strings with units baked in) lives in the server data-access module, so a units or formatting change means editing the data layer rather than the view.
findings.suggestion: Return numeric decimetres/hectograms and format in the component (or a shared display helper), like the em-dash handling already in the views.

findings.issue: Two different search-param mechanisms coexist: the home page uses useLocation().search + manual URLSearchParams while the pokemon page uses useSearchParams (app/src/routes/pokemon/[name].jsx:137), a small consistency cost for future contributors.
findings.suggestion: Standardize on useSearchParams (plus useLocation only for the reactive full search string when needed).

summary: This is a genuinely current SolidStart v2 app, not a training-data-era one: the vite.config/nitro-plugin pairing, engines field, query + "use server" placement, route preload and entrypoints all match the framework's stable October 2026 state exactly, with six lean, all-mandatory dependencies. Data access is centralized in one module and only public APIs are used, so an upgrade would touch few files. What keeps it from a 5 is the absence of any TypeScript at the API boundary, a couple of hand-rolled spots where the platform would do (URL parsing, query-string building), and a status-code-after-stream pattern that upstream still tracks as an open bug.
